label: Slurry, manure, and agricultural effluent management
description: UK legal controls on the storage, handling, spreading, land application, disposal, and pollution prevention of livestock slurry, manure, farmyard manure, poultry manure, pig slurry, liquid manure, silage effluent, agricultural effluent, farm effluent, digestate, and other livestock waste. Core sources include instruments that directly regulate slurry or manure storage infrastructure, silage effluent, agricultural pollution, nitrate vulnerable zones, nutrient action programmes, agricultural diffuse pollution, organic manure application, closed periods, application rates, buffer zones, runoff prevention, and ammonia or water pollution from livestock waste. Treat generic engineering or environmental terms such as freeboard, structural integrity, secondary containment, controlled waters, groundwater protection, buffer zones, and water pollution as supporting signals only: they are not enough on their own unless clearly connected to agricultural slurry, manure, livestock waste, silage effluent, agricultural pollution, or nitrate controls.
synonyms: silage slurry and agricultural fuel oil
exclusions: public roads, traffic, railway, tramway, harbour, gas, water authority or local improvement acts unless they clearly regulate agricultural slurry or manure
plant health or crop disease controls unless they directly regulate manure or slurry spreading as livestock waste management
animal disease controls unless they directly regulate disposal or handling of slurry, manure, or livestock waste
non-UK EU nitrate derogation decisions for Belgium, Denmark, Italy, Netherlands, Germany, Austria, or other non-UK member states
municipal recycling, composting, sewerage or waste targets unless clearly about agricultural livestock waste or farm digestate

metadata.conversion_note: Refined Ada category brief for improved AI triage as well as discovery.

likely_accept: UK, England, Wales, Scotland, or Northern Ireland instruments directly regulating silage, slurry, agricultural fuel oil, slurry storage, agricultural pollution, nitrate pollution, NVZs, nutrient action programmes, or agricultural diffuse pollution.

Principal regulations and important amendment regulations for slurry storage, slurry spreading, manure spreading, organic manure application, closed periods, application rates, buffer zones, and livestock waste pollution prevention.
Foundational assimilated EU or EU-derived instruments only where they underpin UK nitrate, agricultural pollution, or manure/slurry controls.
needs_human_review: Revoked or historical instruments that appear to be predecessors of current slurry, nitrate, or agricultural pollution regimes.
Designation instruments for nitrate vulnerable zones where they define geographical scope rather than substantive duties.
Northern Ireland EU derogation or protocol-related material where post-Brexit applicability is unclear.
Grant schemes or funding instruments that support slurry storage, farm waste, nutrient management, or NVZ compliance.
park_contextual: Animal by-products, digestate, organic fertiliser, BAT, ammonia, waste management, groundwater, or intensive farming material that is adjacent but not primarily about slurry/manure storage or spreading.
Organic farming or fertiliser instruments that mention manure only as a permitted input or nutrient source.
Disease-control instruments that may mention disposal of infected waste but are not primarily environmental slurry/manure controls.
likely_reject: Non-UK EU derogation decisions for other member states under the Nitrates Directive.
Road, railway, tramway, harbour, gas, water authority, local corporation, local improvement, public path, or municipal acts with only incidental manure or effluent references.
Oil storage-only instruments where secondary containment or structural integrity is the only overlap.
Plant health, crop disease, animal disease, public path, construction, shipping, or vehicle safety instruments where category terms are incidental.
triage_guidance.triage_rule: Weak terms are supporting signals only. They must not make a candidate likely_accept unless the title or evidence also clearly connects to slurry, manure, silage effluent, livestock waste, agricultural pollution, nitrate vulnerable zones, or nutrient action programmes.
